thread:
maya: Heads-up — while onboarding `nova-1.0` I spotted a clause that could block redistribution/serving in hosted mode.
srini: can you paste the exact line? is it a non-commercial or attribution thing? :thinking_face:
maya: pasted the snippet below.

maya: ```
Section 4. Redistribution and Use
- You may not redistribute model weights or derivative model artifacts for commercial purposes.
- Any public use must include visible attribution to the original authors as specified in Appendix A.
- Redistribution of quantized or modified weights is explicitly forbidden without express consent.
```

tomas: oof. the "quantized or modified weights" line is the killer for us — that would stop us from shipping a quantized variant or offering dedicated/Dedicated customers a copy.
lina: also attribution in UI is doable but has legal/marketing implications. we should confirm whether "public use" includes our hosted API responses (probably yes).
ops-bot: Note: Private deployments where the customer runs the weights in their infra are often considered redistribution if we bundle the weights for them.

srini: quick questions:
- can we still call the model via an API without rehosting weights? (hosted inference)
- does quantizing for performance count as "modified weights" or internal transform?
- what about embedding-based search indices (are they derivative?)

monica-legal: looping in legal. preliminary read:
- "commercial purposes" needs definition — might allow paid SaaS use if license says so, but many OSS model licenses reject commercial use outright.
- "redistribution" usually covers handing out the weights or posting them; serving via API can still be allowed unless the license says otherwise.
- quantization/derivative: depends on whether license treats transformed weights as "derivative works". some do, some explicitly permit conversions.

maya: thanks. I also noticed Appendix A mentions a required attribution string and a link back to the model repo.

maya: quick mock for how attribution could look in the UI:

maya: "Model: Nova-1.0 (Research Org) — used via Redwood Inference" — is that sufficient?

tomas: might need the exact wording from Appendix A. often they mandate a specific sentence and URL.

lina: until legal confirms, we should stop any plan to publish quantized artifacts or make the weights downloadable in any package.

srini: possible mitigation paths:
- ask upstream for a commercial license or waiver
- host-only: keep weights internal and serve via API (if license allows)
- require Enterprise-only private deployments where customers bring their own weights (BYOW)

monica-legal: action items from my side:
- I will get the full license text and check definitions for "commercial" and "derivative" by EOD.
- If ambiguous, we'll draft an outreach email to the model authors asking for clarification/permission (cc product/legal).

deploy-bot: Link to model card: https://models.example.org/nova-1.0 — license: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 (auto-detected)

srini: CC-BY-NC-SA would prohibit commercial use for sure, and SA causes redistribution headaches — not great.

maya: putting this on the onboarding checklist: stop quantization packaging until legal sign-off. removing the auto-quant job from the pipeline for nova-1.0.

lina: logging note for Product: if upstream requires attribution in all public outputs, we'll need to update docs, SDK, and hosted UI templates.

monica-legal: I'll post back with exact language and recommended product constraints. If they allow "non-commercial only" we should mark model as "internal eval only" and block in hosted/tiered offerings.

maya: thanks — will hold off on further perf experiments until we hear back. :pray:

tomas: thanks all, good catch.
